Instruction: Read the segment of a merger agreement and answer the multiple-choice question by choosing the option that best characterizes the agreement.
Question: Is the “ability to consummate” concept subject to Material Adverse Effect (MAE) carveouts?
Option A: No
Option B: Yes

Merger Agreement: “Material Adverse Effect” means any event, change, occurrence, or effect that, either individually or collectively, has a material adverse impact on the overall business, financial condition, or operational results of the Company and its subsidiaries. For purposes of this Agreement, no effect shall be deemed a Material Adverse Effect if it arises solely from: (a) general fluctuations in economic or market conditions; (b) industry-wide regulatory changes or adjustments in credit ratings that affect all participants; (c) natural disasters, pandemics, or other force majeure events; or (d) delays in closing procedures initiated by mutually agreed factors. Notwithstanding these carveouts, the Agreement expressly provides that any impact on the Company’s ability to consummate the Transaction, including delays or impediments arising from operational setbacks or external market pressures, shall be fully considered within the ambit of a Material Adverse Effect. This explicit qualification indicates that while several aspects are carved out from the MAE definition, the ability to consummate is not shielded by those exceptions. (Pages 12-15)

Question: Is the “ability to consummate” concept subject to Material Adverse Effect (MAE) carveouts?
Option A: No

Merger Agreement: “Material Adverse Effect” means any event, change, occurrence, or effect that, either individually or collectively, has a material adverse impact on the overall business, financial condition, or operational results of the Company and its subsidiaries. For purposes of this Agreement, no effect shall be deemed a Material Adverse Effect if it arises solely from: (a) general fluctuations in economic or market conditions; (b) industry-wide regulatory changes or adjustments in credit ratings that affect all participants; (c) natural disasters, pandemics, or other force majeure events; or (d) delays in closing procedures initiated by mutually agreed factors. In other words, even where other adverse effects are excepted by these provisions, an impairment in the ability to consummate remains fully within the scope of a Company Material Adverse Effect.
